description: One release, without a Dockerfile. Covers Alpine Linux, Debian, Go, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Python and Ubuntu. Give a product and a release — a number like "3.9" or "22.04", a major like Node's "18" or PostgreSQL's "16", or a codename like "jammy" or "bookworm" — and get its release date, its end of active support, its end of security support, the paid extended window where there is one, and a verbatim quote of the vendor's own published line. A release this register does not hold returns found: false rather than a guess.

product.description: One of Alpine Linux, Debian, Go, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Python and Ubuntu, case-insensitive; "node", "nodejs", "golang", "postgres" and "alpine" are accepted too.

release.description: "3.9", "3.11.9", "22.04", a major such as Node's "18" or "v18.17.0" or PostgreSQL's "16", or a codename such as "jammy" or "bookworm".

name: release_support_status

newest_supported_release_we_hold.description: OURS, computed from these records; no source here names a successor.

also_reported.description: Values for this record reported by a SECOND source, each with its own source_url and source_quote. Cite these to the page they name, never to the record's primary source.

covered_by_paid_extended_support.description: OURS, computed: true when free security support has ended but the paid extended window (Ubuntu Pro, Debian ELTS) has not. A caller without that subscription should read this as unsupported.

end_of_active_support.description: The source's eoasFrom date, verbatim. Bug fixes stop here.

end_of_security_support.description: The source's eolFrom date, verbatim. The free security-patch path stops here. This is the date the status is read from.

end_of_support_date_published.description: Whether the source prints an end-of-support date for this release at all. False where the source only marks the release ended (Node.js 1 to 3, PostgreSQL 6.0 to 6.2) or still maintained (Go's two newest majors), so "supported" with no date can be told from "supported until a stated date".

extended_security_maintenance.description: Ubuntu and Debian only: the source's eoesFrom date, verbatim. This is cover that has to be bought or comes from somebody other than the publisher — Ubuntu Pro's Expanded Security Maintenance, Debian's ELTS — so it is NOT treated as support when computing the status.

product.description: The product name as the source writes it: one of Alpine Linux, Debian, Go, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Python and Ubuntu.

record_url.description: This record's own page on referencesource.org.

release.description: The release label exactly as the source writes it, e.g. "3.11", "24.04 'Noble Numbat' (LTS)", "12 (Bookworm)", "22 (LTS)".

released.description: Release date, verbatim from the source.

source_quote.description: Verbatim text from that page containing the value.

source_url.description: The page the value was read from.

status.description: OURS, computed against the date of the call: "supported", "past end of active support", "past end of security support", or "no end-of-support date published". The dates above are the vendor's.

status_basis.description: OURS: what the status was read from — "eol", "eoas", or, for a release the source prints no end date for, which of its own flags said the release had ended or was still maintained.

under_review.description: PRESENT ONLY when a re-reading of this record's own source page states a different value from the one published here. Each named field's value is unsettled and must be cited as disputed, not as the publisher's current position. Absent means no correction is on file for this record — it is never returned empty.

reported_on.description: The date we re-read the page.

reported_value_found_in_that_quote.description: Whether the NEW value was found verbatim inside the new quote. False means the re-reading is not itself quote-confirmed.

vendor_names_for_these_dates.description: The source's own labels object, verbatim.

smallest_step_up_we_hold.description: OURS, computed from these records: the LOWEST release above this one that is still getting free security fixes — usually the cheaper move, and not always the newest. It can be a release whose ACTIVE support has already ended, so read `status` and `end_of_security_support` before offering it: security fixes only is a shorter runway than full support. Absent when there is nothing above this release to move to, or when the only thing above it is the release already named in newest_supported_release_we_hold.

end_of_security_support.description: The date free security fixes for the step up stop, verbatim from the source.

note.description: What this answer is and what it is not, in words.

release.description: The release label as the source writes it.

status.description: This step up's own status today: "supported" or "past end of active support".

title: Is this release still supported?
